transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what brought me in is that some evenings after work... I've been having this issue where I end up eating way more than I meant to. It usually happens when I've been really strict with myself all day. I'll have my regular dinner, but then I just keep going—I'll have cereal, crackers, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and then sweets. And this all happens within just a couple of hours. I figured I should probably come in and talk to someone about it.
After one of these episodes of eating a large amount, do you ever try to make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting the next day, or exercising a lot to compensate?

No, I don't make myself throw up or use laxatives or anything like that. But... yeah, the next day after one of those nights, I definitely tell myself I need to make up for it. I'll usually just skip breakfast and lunch entirely. Or I'll go out for an extra-long hike, or make sure I push a lot harder at my softball conditioning... even when I'm already really tired. I just feel like I have to do something to balance it out.
Over the past few months, how many times per week would you say these binge-eating episodes have been happening?

Well, looking at the past few months, I'd say it's been happening most weeks. It's usually about one or two nights a week where I end up eating far more than I planned to. And then, yeah, the very next day is when I try to make up for it by skipping meals or exercising a lot longer.
Would you say that your sense of self-worth or how you feel about yourself is strongly tied to your body shape or weight?

Yeah, I'd say it is. It definitely affects how I feel about myself. Like, if I'm getting dressed for work and my waistband feels tight before a client luncheon or a leadership meeting... I just start feeling like I look sloppy. I get worried that people won't take me as seriously, even though I know I've still been doing my job just fine. It just really bothers me and messes with my confidence.
You mentioned this has been happening 'the past few months'—can you tell me exactly how many months this pattern of binge eating followed by skipping meals or excessive exercise has been going on?
I'd say it's been about four months now. It started right after the agency went through a regional sales reorganization. So, yeah, it's been going on for four months.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and whether your weight has changed significantly over the past few months?
I'm about 5'5", and I usually weigh around 140 pounds. My weight hasn't really changed much over the past few months, honestly. It stays pretty consistent, even with everything going on.
